antipatterns: tests/Feature/OrdersApiTest.php:131 - uses a foreach over responses where a Pest dataset would be clearer, and a single failing response can't be identified

strengths: The only implementation that orders CheckAbilities before SubstituteBindings (bootstrap/app.php:21). A token without the read ability gets 403 whether the order exists or not, so status codes reveal nothing about which IDs exist. Probing confirmed this
OrderPolicy::view uses Response::denyAsNotFound() together with the can:view,order route middleware. This is the idiomatic way to return 404 for another user's order

The 404 render keys on HttpException status. It turns ModelNotFound and route-miss responses into a generic 'Not found.', so with debug off the 'No query results for model [App\Models\Order]' message is never shown
Casts total_cents to integer, so the JSON type is consistent even for form-encoded input. Uses the #[Fillable] attribute, casts() method, HasMany relation and a composite (user_id, created_at) index
Tests call forgetGuards() in the token helper, which avoids the Sanctum guard-caching trap when several tokens are used in one test. Tests cover requests with no Accept header for 401, 422 and 201
The rule user()->orders()->create() means a user_id sent in the body is ignored, and a test covers this

bugs: Order has no integer cast on total_cents. A form-encoded POST (common for scripts that send no Accept or Content-Type) returns "total_cents":"5" as a string in the 201 body, while JSON input returns an int, so the API contract's type is inconsistent (confirmed by probe)

Enables RefreshDatabase in Pest.php, and the resource omits updated_at to keep the payload lean

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-1 first, impl-2 second and impl-3 third. All three test suites pass (19, 29 and 19 tests). All three handle the basics: 401 JSON with no Accept header (via redirectGuestsTo), JSON 422 responses, 201 on create, owner-scoped listing newest first at 20 per page, and a generic 'Not found.' 404 that hides the 'No query results for model [App\Models\Order]' message when debug is off.

My first probe was invalid because the Sanctum guard caches the first token's user across requests in one test. I reran it with forgetGuards() between calls. The rerun showed two differences.

impl-3 has a real problem in the task's focus area. Route model binding runs before the ability middleware, so a token without orders:read gets 404 for an order that doesn't exist but 403 for another user's existing order. Any token can use that difference to find out which order IDs exist. This breaks 'answer 404 for it, the same as for an order that doesn't exist'.

impl-1 uses the same policy and binding design but fixes the problem explicitly with prependToPriorityList, and its tests check it. It is also free of the other issues: total_cents is cast to integer and the guest redirect is scoped to the API.

impl-2 avoids the oracle without trying to, because it calls findOrFail in the controller after the ability check. But it has no integer cast, so form-encoded creates return total_cents as the string "5". Its show method also skips route model binding.

impl-3 has the strongest tests, but bugs carry the most weight here. Its existence oracle breaks a stated security requirement, while impl-2's bug is a type inconsistency in the response, so impl-3 ranks below impl-2.
